videos.headline: Toyota vs Mercedes (the Lexus story) passed 1,200 views and held 75.8% of it.

why.text: 1,215 views in 48 hours against the Shorts median of 670.5.
75.8% viewed against the median of 54.9%; 57.8% stayed to watch against 44.2%.
22.1 points left at 5.5 s on "Its own best customers got richer, and traded up to Mercedes and BMW".

videos.next: Rivalry hooks work here; make the second beat the secret plan (the 450 prototypes) rather than the background.

videos.headline: Krispy Kreme and McDonald's is the channel's biggest Short: 1,529 views, 78.2% viewed.

why.text: 1,529 views in 48 hours against the Shorts median of 670.5.
78.2% viewed against the median of 54.9%; 57.8% stayed to watch.
16 points left at 1.5 s on the hook and 13.2 at 7.8 s on the 13,500-restaurant line.

videos.next: Two famous brands breaking up is a format to repeat; open on the break-up itself, the hook lost 16 points before the deal was told.

videos.headline: Spanx reached 72 views and only a third stayed to watch.

why.text: 72 views in 48 hours against the Shorts median of 670.5.
33.9% stayed to watch against the median of 44.2%; 60% viewed.
Viewers fell 14.3 points three times: at 2.6 s, 6.6 s and 17.8 s, on a small sample of 74 views.

videos.next: A founder's savings figure was a weaker hook than a rivalry or break-up here; lead with the conflict or the twist.

videos.headline: The Crocs long video has 49 views and a 2.5% click rate.

why.text: 49 views; 77.8% came from related videos.

32.2% viewed of a 15-minute video.

videos.next: Test a thumbnail with the shoe itself and one number; the click rate, not the watch, is what holds it back.

videos.headline: Marvel's Captain America collateral kept viewers (54.5% stayed) but reached only 232.

videos.next: Show what Marvel put up (the characters as collateral) before saying it went bankrupt.
